headline: Global Hunger Falls Below 8% for First Time Since Pandemic
meta_description: For the third consecutive year, global malnourishment has declined, dropping below 8% of the population for the first time since COVID-19 disruptions ended.
summary_short: Global hunger reaches its lowest point ever recorded, falling below 8% for the first time since the pandemic. Asia's steep five-year decline is leading the way.
body:
For the third consecutive year, global malnourishment has declined significantly, with the latest UN Food and Agriculture Organization report showing that just 7.8% of the world's population is now considered malnourished. This marks the first time since government-enforced business closures and pandemic supply disruptions that the figure has fallen below 8%—and represents a historic milestone. The improvement is particularly striking when measured against 1970, when undernourishment afflicted nearly 35% of people living outside Europe and North America. The FAO predicts this figure will drop another 20% by the end of the decade, potentially marking the lowest hunger level ever recorded in human history.

Asia has emerged as the engine of this progress. Central Asia exemplifies the transformation, with malnourishment plummeting from 7.7% to just 2.8% since 2010—matching the levels of high-income countries. Southeast Asia has achieved similarly dramatic results, falling from 11.6% to 5.1% over the same period. The Caribbean and Latin America have also contributed to the downward trend, though gains have been more modest than in Asia.

Yet the global picture remains uneven. Africa continues to struggle with the world's highest hunger rates, with some regions exceeding 20% malnourishment, concentrated primarily in conflict zones. This reveals a sobering truth: warfare remains the strongest driver of hunger worldwide, with West Asia and Central and Eastern Africa hit hardest. The data suggests an encouraging possibility—if wars can be brought to an end, the progress witnessed in rural Central Asia could be replicated across these vulnerable regions, potentially unlocking dramatic improvements in food security for millions.
quick_facts: 7.8% of global population is malnourished, lowest since pandemic began
Central Asia reduced malnourishment from 7.7% to 2.8% since 2010
Hunger predicted to drop another 20% by end of decade
Africa remains most undernourished continent at 20%+ in some regions
Conflict is the strongest driver of malnourishment worldwide
